base table is always present and referenced.

result.response:
I have resolved the issue where `Model.objects.all().delete()` generated a subquery by ensuring the query's base table is initialized in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-s2wqa3b0/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1407-L1412) in [django/db/models/sql/compiler.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-s2wqa3b0/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py).

### Cause
When a `QuerySet` without filters (such as `Model.objects.all()`) was fast-deleted, `self.query.alias_map` was still empty when [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-s2wqa3b0/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) was evaluated, causing `single_alias` to evaluate to `False` (`0 == 1`) and fall back to wrapping the query in a subquery (`DELETE FROM ... WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM ...)`).

### Fix
Call `self.query.get_initial_alias()` in [`SQLDeleteCompiler.single_alias`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-s2wqa3b0/django/db/models/sql/compiler.py#L1408-L1412) prior to checking `alias_refcount` so the base table is always present and referenced.
